title: Technical Deep Dive - BroWerk (DE) private + residency
summary: German enterprise evaluating Private. Clear requirement: data sovereignty, no US processing or support access; prefer Germany region and in-country logging.
next_steps: Redwood to share Private reference architecture
Customer to confirm whether EU-only is sufficient or Germany-only is required
Set up workshop on logging/metrics in-country
transcript:
Meeting: Technical Deep Dive - BroWerk (DE) private + residency
Date: 2025-02-18
Duration: 47 min

[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hi Klara, Jan. Today is a technical deep dive on Private and requirements.
[00:10] Klara (BroWerk): Great. Were running pilots internally.

[01:05] Jan (BroWerk): Straight to the point: we need data sovereignty. Our legal team says prompts and outputs cannot be processed in the US, and ideally not even accessible by US-based support.
[01:25] Hannah (Redwood): Understood. For Private in your VPC, you control the network and access. Support access is through your approved channels, usually temporary and logged.

[03:10] Klara: We prefer Germany-only if possible. EU-only might be acceptable but we need to check.
[03:20] Alex: Okay. So residency is either Germany-only preferred, EU-only as fallback.

[07:40] Jan: Also logs. Any audit logs or traces should be stored in Germany.
[07:52] Hannah: Thats typical with Private. We can integrate with your SIEM and keep it in-country.

[15:05] Klara: Control plane: does anything phone home?
[15:12] Hannah: Private can be configured with restricted egress. Well document what components need outbound access and alternatives.

[32:30] Jan: Weve had vendors say EU region but then model updates or telemetry goes to US. We cant do that.
[32:43] Alex: Got it. Well be explicit in the architecture and contract language about region pinning and data flow.

[46:10] Alex: Next steps: well send the reference architecture and schedule a workshop on residency + logging.
